lessons.text: When the 1h, 4h and 24h USOON returns are all the same value, USOON printed once and then froze. Treat it like an all-zero stale quote (L38) and wait for the US open to check against USO.

Before the US open, a 4h gap under 1% with a cost near 0.9% can never pass. Settle it quickly using the L51 fair-value estimate (USO close × perp move) and save web searches for after 13:30 UTC, when live USO data exists.
With 20 minutes to the US open and a stale USOON print, skip and recheck once USO trades. Pre-open entries against a frozen quote keep scoring about −0.5% to −0.9% net at 1–4h.

Right after the US open, a 1h perp spike against a USOON print with zero returns is still a stale quote. Compare the ask with USO close × (1 + the perp's move since the close) before calling USOON cheap. At 13:45 UTC the ask was about 1.8%

In US hours, when USOON is updating but lags a 1% perp hour, estimate fair value as USO close × (1 + the perp's move since 20:00 UTC) before treating it as a lag. Here the ask was already near that value.

During US hours, measure the USOON ask against the previous USO close before reading the perp gap. Here a 24h perp rally of about 4% already left the ask 2.4% above the USO close, which absorbs most of the apparent 4h lag.
During US hours, if the 1h gap is positive (USOON ahead) and the 4h gap is below the cost, a trigger that leans on the 24h gap is noise. Skip it without searching.

lessons.text: During off-hours, if the 1h, 4h and 24h USOON returns are all the same value, one print moved the quote. Treat it as stale (L38) and anchor fair value on USO's close × (1 + the perp move since then).
Pre-open triggers with a 4h gap below 1% and a cost near 0.9% have kept scoring negative. Skip them without searching, and recheck USO against the USOON ask after 13:30 UTC instead.

At 20 minutes before the open with a frozen USOON print, do not search widely. Wait for the first post-open snapshot and compare it with live USO (L41), because pre-open skips have kept scoring negative net.

At the US open, a perp spike of about 1% in 1h with a 4h gap under 1.5% does not make USOON cheap. Recheck it against USO close × (1 + perp move since 20:00) after 1–2 live bars, before treating it as a lag.

In the first hour of the US session, a perp burst of about 1% with a 4h gap under 1.5% only gives a USO-close-based fair-value discount of roughly 0.2–0.6%. Without a live USO quote that is about the size of the cost, so skip it rather than

Even during US hours, USOON's 1h return can read exactly 0 while the perp moves. Treat that as a stale print (L38), not a lag. Recheck after the next USOON print, and enter only if the gap stays above 1.5% once the quote is updating.

During US hours, a trigger whose 1h gap is positive (perp falling while USOON is flat) and whose 4h gap is under 1% is noise. Skip it without searching, unless there is a new headline after the US open.

During US hours, a 4h perp gap above 1.5% on a strong rally day was again absorbed: USO (~167.5) sat just below the USOON ask (168.0). Check the USO quote first; if the USOON ask is at or above USO's intraday high, skip.

On 23 Oct, a 4h perp gap of 1.6–1.8% again turned out to be no edge once checked against live USO (Robinhood $168.32 vs ask 167.99). This confirms L41: the perp's 24h move already includes USO's catch-up from the prior close.
Once the trigger's 4h perp gap is below 1.5% and the last known USO price is below the USOON ask, skip the web search. The rule and the USO check settle it for free.
When the 4h gap is under 1.5% and USOON's returns read 0, skip without searching. Before any buy, check live USO against the USOON ask.
